todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.
outcome: Finish task 004 by durably recording a removal cutoff for shared-access conversations without dropping their valid follow, and by synchronizing cleanup enumeration through the Messaging-owned cleanup checkpoint so an interleaved stale root cannot restore a follow.
scope: Revise the current task-004 candidate in place. Retain its Club-owned membership generations, Messaging-owned `MemberFollowEligibility` cutoff stream, success-only sender-follow policy, retained-newer-follow event semantics, public Membership-to-Messaging cleanup boundary, and custom-group add/remove completion contract.

Change the shared-access branch of `Memba.Messaging.clear_removed_group_member_follow/7`: when another active group still grants authoritative conversation access, preserve the current follow but still dispatch an idempotent cleanup command/fact that records this removal generation in `Memba.Messaging.ConversationFollowers`. Do not encode preservation only as `cleanup_generation < current_follow_generation`; shared access can require retention when the generations are equal.

Keep effective-access union semantics intact. The surviving group continues to authorize and retain the shared follow, while the removed group's cutoff remains durable after an ordinary unfollow. Delayed manual or reply-auto work at or before that removal generation must then be rejected, and genuinely newer post-re-add follow work must remain allowed.

Make `Memba.Messaging.clear_removed_group_member_follows/2` wait its Message, conversation-access, and conversation-follow projectors through a durable checkpoint at or after the newly appended `MemberFollowCleanupRecorded`, not only through the originating Membership `GroupMemberRemoved` checkpoint. Preserve idempotent event-free retries by deriving or retaining a safe cleanup checkpoint when `RecordMemberFollowCleanup` emits no new event.

Add deterministic integration proof for the exact interleaving: a stale root `MessageSent` commits after the Membership removal checkpoint but before `MemberFollowCleanupRecorded`; its sender-follow policy reads the old eligibility state; its conversation is still unprojected at the old checkpoint; cleanup must not acknowledge until projectors cross the Messaging cleanup checkpoint, must discover and cut off the conversation, and must leave no effective follow.

Update shared/unrelated-access tests so the unrelated-only conversation receives no cleanup fact, while the shared conversation remains followed and receives one retained, idempotent cutoff fact. Then ordinarily unfollow it and prove delayed pre-removal manual and actual reply-auto follow work cannot restore it.

Keep and rerun the current focused proof for manual/root/reply sources, newer-follow retention, cleanup-before-later-stream creation, blank/duplicate reply rejection, remove/re-add races, projection lag, replay/idempotency, dispatch options, caller-selected return modes, unrelated follows, and Everyone/Admin no-ops.
scope_exclusions: Do not replace task 004 with a new task or reset its revision identity. All three prior candidate origins remain cumulative and unresolved until review accepts this obligation.

Do not weaken effective-access union by requiring every conversation group to pass member-level eligibility. A valid surviving group still grants access; the missing invariant is the durable per-conversation cutoff for the removed group.

Do not change task 001's accepted removal authorization, actor/target validation, self/last-member behavior, club role/membership preservation, system-group rejection, or `GroupMemberRemoved`-only transition semantics except for backward-compatible task-004 ordering data.

Do not revisit already-closed prior gaps unless a regression requires it: success-only reply auto-follow, conversations created after fully acknowledged cleanup, retained newer follows, explicit consistency lists, and supported Commanded return shapes already have candidate coverage.
Do not implement broader group/conversation read or action authorization, queued-delivery/provider-handoff reauthorization, or open-LiveView refresh assigned to tasks 009-011.
Do not add Leave/Remove UI, confirmations, shared member-row changes, post-removal screens, or empty-group UI behavior assigned to tasks 012-014.
Do not edit iteration-064 feature files or implement the browser/domain acceptance layer assigned to tasks 015-016.

Do not mutate Membership projections from Messaging or Messaging projections from Membership, use transient process caches for ordering, or directly write projection tables. Preserve public context APIs and durable commands/facts.
Do not redesign unrelated delivery, conversation authorization, multi-group editing, projection infrastructure, or club role lifecycle.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, browser acceptance, or another unscoped full-suite command; task 017 and the deterministic `dev_check` node own the final repository gate.

references.facts: Implementation Plan 2 and the acceptance/open-technical-decision text require public Messaging APIs, idempotent facts, all follow sources, stale remove/re-add safety, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behavior.
Iteration 062 established the replay-safe Membership-to-Messaging cleanup collaboration and requires departure/rejoin ordering; task 004 extends that boundary to explicit custom-group removal.
Membership owns group membership and Messaging owns follow state. Coordination uses public context APIs rather than another context's aggregates or projection storage.
The Club stream is authoritative for membership lifecycle and preserves historic facts; system-group membership remains a downstream policy consequence.

`clear_removed_group_member_follow/7` currently returns `:ok` when another group preserves access, skipping the `UnfollowConversation` cutoff entirely. `clear_removed_group_member_follows/2` appends `MemberFollowCleanupRecorded` but calls `await_removed_group_follow_cleanup_projections/1` with the earlier Membership checkpoint.

`ConversationFollowers` already keeps cleanup generations across ordinary unfollow and supports retained cleanup facts, but retention currently derives only from an older cleanup generation; shared access needs an explicit durable retain-with-cutoff contract.
Member-level eligibility correctly permits a follow through any surviving access group. It cannot replace the missing conversation-specific cutoff after shared access and an ordinary unfollow.

The strong sender-follow policy reads Messaging-owned eligibility after `MessageSent`. The new interleaving test must prove cleanup catches stale work accepted before `MemberFollowCleanupRecorded` but not yet visible at the older Membership checkpoint.

The origin-replaying handler supplies the Membership removal event identity, generation, and event-number checkpoint to the public Messaging cleanup API. Preserve origin replay and direct Everyone/Admin no-op behavior.

The shared-access test currently expects zero cleanup events on the shared conversation, and the late-root test dispatches only after cleanup fully returns. Update the former and add a deterministic between-checkpoints interleaving using existing handler suspension, projector stop/restart, barriers, and `Task.yield/2` patterns.

Current retained-cutoff coverage proves only cleanup generation 5 against follow generation 6. Add aggregate proof that explicit shared-access retention records a cutoff without dropping an equal-generation valid follow and survives ordinary unfollow.
Commands/events remain the write authority; lagging read projections may guide enumeration only after the required durable checkpoint.
Ordering and replay behavior must be represented by durable, backward-compatible facts rather than ephemeral workflow memory or projection-only state.
Use deterministic synchronization such as supervised processes, handler suspension, monitors, `Task.yield/2`, and state/barrier checks rather than sleeps.

constraints: Keep task identity 004 and revise the existing candidate; do not invent another task for the same rejected obligation.

Use Club-owned membership history as the causal source and Messaging-owned event-sourced state as the follow authority. Do not query another context's aggregate internals or directly write projection tables.
Every relevant shared conversation must durably record the removed-group cutoff while retaining a currently valid shared follow. An unrelated conversation must remain untouched.
Ordinary user unfollow remains distinct from membership cleanup and must not erase prior cleanup generations or completed cleanup IDs.
Delayed work at or before the removed generation must remain rejected after ordinary unfollow; a valid follow above the cutoff after genuine re-add must remain possible.
The enumeration barrier must cover a durable Messaging checkpoint at or after `MemberFollowCleanupRecorded`; preserve safe behavior when an exact retry emits no new cleanup event.

The interleaving regression must be deterministic and prove the stale root commits between the Membership removal and Messaging cleanup facts while relevant projections remain behind. Avoid timing sleeps.

Preserve backward replay of historic `GroupMemberAdded`, `GroupMemberRemoved`, `MessageSent`, `ConversationFollowed`, `ConversationUnfollowed`, and cleanup shapes with absent generation/retention fields.
Preserve `ClearRemovedGroupMemberFollows` origin replay while ensuring ordinary projector reset/replay does not dispatch cross-context side effects.

Preserve successful public add/remove return semantics and cleanup completion for default, `:strong`, `:eventual`, explicit handler lists, event-free exact retry, and supported caller-selected Commanded return options.
Limit edits to durable shared-conversation cutoff semantics, cleanup checkpoint synchronization, and their focused tests. Leave tasks 009-017 untouched.
completion_evidence_required: List changed paths and describe the durable command/event state used to retain a valid shared follow while recording the removed-group per-conversation cutoff, including replay and historic absent-field behavior.
Describe how `clear_removed_group_member_follows/2` obtains and waits through the Messaging cleanup checkpoint, including event-free exact-retry handling.
Report exit statuses and test counts for both focused test commands on the exact handoff state, plus `git diff --check`.

Identify an integration test proving a shared conversation stays followed yet records one idempotent cutoff, an unrelated-only conversation receives none, ordinary unfollow preserves the cutoff, and delayed older manual plus actual reply-auto work cannot restore the follow.

Identify a deterministic test proving a stale root commits after the Membership removal checkpoint and before `MemberFollowCleanupRecorded`, remains unprojected at the old checkpoint, prevents cleanup acknowledgement until projectors cross the Messaging checkpoint, and ends without an effective sender follow.

Show genuinely newer post-re-add follows remain allowed and existing retained-newer-follow, manual/root/reply source, cleanup-before-later-stream, projection-lag, replay/idempotency, explicit-list/return-mode, and Everyone/Admin no-op tests still pass.

Confirm accepted task-001 behavior remains unchanged: explicit removal emits only the reusable Membership removal fact for a transition, exact retry emits no new Membership fact, and club membership/roles plus system-group guards are preserved.

latest_review.summary: Record the removed-group cutoff even when shared access preserves the follow, and synchronize one-time conversation enumeration through the durable Messaging cleanup checkpoint so a stale root committed between cleanup facts cannot restore a follow.

latest_worker_result.summary: The candidate added member-scoped durable cleanup cutoffs, retained-newer-follow facts, success-only sender-follow orchestration, return/consistency coverage, and reported 38- and 79-test focused suites passing; the latest review found the remaining shared-access cutoff and between-checkpoints enumeration gaps described above.
